outputs.L1: The invention relates to an apparatus designed and configured to stun live poultry intended for slaughter while housed in containers, using a gas mixture comprising a stunning gas. The apparatus comprises a stunning chamber having at least two stunning zones; an introduction station arranged on the inlet side of the stunning chamber for the or each container holding live poultry; a discharge station arranged on the outlet side of the stunning chamber for the or each container holding stunned poultry; at least one transport conveyor configured to transport the or each container in the transport direction T through the stunning zones, from the introduction station to the discharge station; and means for delivering the gas mixture into the stunning zones of the stunning chamber. The apparatus is characterised in that the means for delivering the gas mixture comprises at least one injection pipe designed and configured to move relative to the container, to establish a detachable connection to the or each container, and to detach therefrom, such that each container can be filled with the gas mixture while detachably connected to the or each injection pipe. The invention further relates to an arrangement comprising such an apparatus and at least one container, as well as to a corresponding method.
outputs.L2:
The invention concerns equipment for stunning live poultry kept in containers and intended for slaughter, using a gas mixture that includes a stunning agent. The equipment includes a stunning chamber divided into at least two stunning zones; an entry station on the chamber’s inlet side for receiving one or more containers holding live birds; an exit station on the outlet side for one or more containers holding stunned birds; at least one conveyor that moves each container in transport direction T from the entry station, through the stunning zones, to the exit station; and a system for supplying the gas mixture to the chamber’s stunning zones.

The equipment is distinguished by a gas-supply system incorporating at least one injection pipe. This pipe is movable relative to the container and is configured to be temporarily coupled to, and subsequently disconnected from, each container. While coupled to the injection pipe or pipes, each container can be filled with the gas mixture.

The invention also encompasses an assembly comprising this equipment together with at least one container, as well as a corresponding stunning method.
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to an apparatus for stunning live poultry intended for slaughter while the animals remain inside their transport containers. The apparatus comprises a stunning chamber divided into at least two stunning zones, together with an inlet introduction station for receiving the poultry containers and an outlet discharge station for removing them after stunning.

At least one conveyor is provided to transport the containers from the introduction station, through the successive stunning zones, and onward to the discharge station. During this process, a movable injection pipe is detachably connected to each container. The pipe introduces a gas mixture containing a suitable stunning gas into the container, thereby stunning the poultry without requiring the animals to be unloaded beforehand.

The invention further encompasses an arrangement comprising the stunning apparatus in combination with at least one poultry container configured for use with the movable injection pipe. It also covers a corresponding method in which a container holding live poultry is introduced into the apparatus, conveyed through the stunning zones, supplied with a stunning-gas mixture via the detachably connected injection pipe, and subsequently discharged after the poultry has been stunned.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to the controlled-atmosphere stunning of live poultry while the birds remain in transport containers. An installation is provided with a multi-zone stunning chamber through which the poultry-filled containers are conveyed. The chamber may include successive treatment zones in which the composition, concentration, flow rate, temperature, and exposure time of a stunning gas mixture can be controlled to produce gradual induction and maintenance of unconsciousness.

A conveyor system transports each container into, through, and out of the chamber. One or more movable gas-injection pipes are arranged along the conveyor path. As a container reaches a treatment position, the corresponding pipe moves into engagement with a gas inlet of the container and forms a detachable connection. The stunning gas mixture is then supplied directly to the interior of the container rather than merely being released into the surrounding chamber. Before the container advances to the next position or leaves the chamber, the pipe is disconnected and returned to a position that allows unobstructed movement of the containers.

The detachable connection may be formed automatically and may include a sealing arrangement that limits leakage between the pipe and the container inlet. Separate pipes or gas-supply circuits may be associated with different zones, permitting each zone to deliver a selected gas mixture or concentration. The timing of container movement and pipe engagement can be coordinated by a control system so that the birds receive a predetermined treatment sequence. Gas may also be discharged or extracted through one or more container outlets, thereby promoting controlled circulation through the space occupied by the birds.

The associated container arrangement includes at least one inlet configured to cooperate with a movable injection pipe. The inlet may incorporate a valve, closure, coupling, or other interface that opens when connected and closes after disconnection. The container can therefore retain the birds during loading, transport, stunning, and subsequent handling, reducing or eliminating the need to remove conscious birds from the transport container before stunning.

In operation, a container holding live poultry is placed on the conveyor and introduced into the stunning chamber. At a selected zone, an injection pipe is moved into sealed communication with the container inlet. A controlled quantity of stunning gas is supplied directly into the container for a predetermined period. The pipe is then detached, and the container is conveyed onward. This process may be repeated in successive zones with different gas compositions or concentrations until the birds have reached and maintained the required state of unconsciousness.

By filling the containers directly, the system provides more accurate control over the atmosphere experienced by the poultry and reduces dependence on the gas concentration in the chamber as a whole. The arrangement can improve treatment uniformity, reduce gas consumption and leakage, and support continuous or indexed processing. The invention accordingly encompasses the stunning apparatus, the transport-container and coupling arrangement, and the method of stunning poultry by conveying loaded containers through multiple treatment zones while detachably connecting movable injection pipes to the containers to deliver the stunning gas mixture.
outputs.L5:
### The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an essential role in communication. It is known as the definite article and is used to identify a particular person, place, object, or idea. For example, “a book” may refer to any book, while “the book” points to a specific one.

Although it often goes unnoticed, “the” gives language clarity and precision. It helps speakers and writers distinguish what is known from what is new or general. This simple three-letter word demonstrates that even the most ordinary parts of language can have a powerful purpose.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for an apparatus that stuns live poultry in transport containers using a gas mixture delivered through movable injection pipes that detachably connect to each container.
counterfactuals.output: An apparatus for stunning live poultry held in transport containers comprises a gas-supply system configured to deliver a stunning gas mixture to the containers and a plurality of movable injection pipes in fluid communication with the gas-supply system. Each injection pipe is movable between a disengaged position and an operating position in which the pipe is detachably connected to a corresponding container through a gas inlet. A positioning mechanism aligns and couples the injection pipes with respective containers while permitting subsequent disconnection and removal of the containers. The apparatus may include valves and a controller configured to regulate the composition, flow rate, pressure, and delivery duration of the gas mixture independently or collectively for the containers. The gas mixture is introduced into each container in an amount and for a period sufficient to stun the poultry before further handling or processing, while reducing the need to remove conscious poultry from the transport containers.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a European-style patent summary describing a multi-zone poultry stunning chamber with introduction and discharge stations, a conveyor, and container-specific gas injection means. Also mention the associated arrangement and method.
counterfactuals.output: The invention relates to a poultry stunning chamber comprising an introduction station, a discharge station and a plurality of stunning zones arranged therebetween. A conveyor is configured to transport containers holding poultry from the introduction station, through the stunning zones, to the discharge station. Each stunning zone comprises gas injection means controllable in relation to an individual container, such that a selected stunning gas composition, concentration and/or flow rate can be supplied to or around the respective container independently of another container present in the chamber. The chamber may further comprise sensors and a control unit for controlling gas injection on the basis of container position, poultry characteristics and/or measured atmospheric conditions. The invention also relates to an arrangement comprising the stunning chamber and a poultry-processing line, and to a method comprising conveying poultry-containing containers through successive stunning zones and container-specifically controlling gas injection to establish a predetermined stunning regime.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate patent claim-style text for an apparatus, arrangement, and method for stunning poultry intended for slaughter while the birds remain in containers, emphasizing the detachable connection between the gas-delivery pipe and each container.
counterfactuals.output:
### Claims

1. **An apparatus for stunning poultry intended for slaughter while the poultry remain in a container, the apparatus comprising:**  
   a container configured to receive and retain a plurality of live poultry;  
   a gas inlet associated with the container; and  
   a gas-delivery pipe configured to convey a stunning gas to the gas inlet,  
   wherein the gas-delivery pipe is detachably connectable to the container such that the gas-delivery pipe is connected to the container during delivery of the stunning gas and is removable from the container after stunning without removing the poultry from the container.

2. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the detachable connection comprises a releasable coupling forming a substantially gas-tight seal between the gas-delivery pipe and the gas inlet.

3. The apparatus of claim 2, wherein the releasable coupling comprises at least one of a quick-release coupling, bayonet coupling, threaded coupling, snap-fit coupling, clamping coupling, or plug-and-socket coupling.

4. The apparatus of any preceding claim, wherein the gas inlet includes a normally closed valve configured to open upon connection of the gas-delivery pipe and to close upon detachment of the gas-delivery pipe.

5. The apparatus of any preceding claim, wherein the gas-delivery pipe includes a shutoff valve configured to inhibit discharge of stunning gas when the gas-delivery pipe is detached from the container.

6. The apparatus of any preceding claim, further comprising a gas outlet arranged to discharge air displaced from the container during introduction of the stunning gas.

7. The apparatus of any preceding claim, wherein the container includes one or more ventilation openings and a closure arrangement operable to restrict gas flow through the ventilation openings during stunning.

8. The apparatus of any preceding claim, wherein the container is transportable and is configured to remain mechanically separate from a fixed gas-supply installation when the gas-delivery pipe is detached.

9. The apparatus of any preceding claim, wherein the stunning gas comprises carbon dioxide, an inert gas, a reduced-oxygen gas mixture, or a combination thereof.

10. **An arrangement for stunning poultry intended for slaughter, the arrangement comprising:**  
    a plurality of containers, each container being configured to hold live poultry and including a respective gas inlet;  
    a gas-supply system configured to supply a stunning gas; and  
    at least one gas-delivery pipe fluidly connected to the gas-supply system,  
    wherein the at least one gas-delivery pipe is selectively and detachably connectable to the respective gas inlet of each container to deliver the stunning gas into the container while the poultry remain therein.

11. The arrangement of claim 10, comprising a plurality of gas-delivery pipes, each gas-delivery pipe being detachably connectable to a corresponding one of the plurality of containers to permit simultaneous delivery of stunning gas to the plurality of containers.

12. The arrangement of claim 10 or 11, wherein the containers are supported in a stacked, racked, or side-by-side configuration during delivery of the stunning gas.

13. The arrangement of any of claims 10–12, further comprising a manifold disposed between a source of stunning gas and the at least one gas-delivery pipe.

14. The arrangement of claim 13, wherein the manifold includes independently controllable valves for regulating gas flow to respective containers.

15. The arrangement of any of claims 10–14, further comprising a connection sensor configured to detect whether the gas-delivery pipe is secured to the respective gas inlet.

16. The arrangement of claim 15, further comprising a controller configured to permit gas delivery only when the connection sensor indicates that the gas-delivery pipe is secured to the respective gas inlet.

17. The arrangement of any of claims 10–16, further comprising at least one sensor configured to measure, within at least one container, a gas concentration, oxygen concentration, pressure, temperature, or combination thereof.

18. The arrangement of claim 17, wherein a controller regulates gas flow to the at least one container in response to an output of the at least one sensor.

19. The arrangement of any of claims 10–18, wherein detachment of the gas-delivery pipe permits the respective container, together with stunned poultry contained therein, to be transported away from the gas-supply system.

20. **A method of stunning poultry intended for slaughter, the method comprising:**  
    placing live poultry in a container;  
    detachably connecting a gas-delivery pipe to a gas inlet of the container;  
    supplying a stunning gas through the gas-delivery pipe and the gas inlet into the container while the poultry remain in the container;  
    maintaining a stunning atmosphere in the container for a time sufficient to stun the poultry;  
    terminating the supply of stunning gas; and  
    detaching the gas-delivery pipe from the container while the stunned poultry remain in the container.

21. The method of claim 20, further comprising transporting the container to a slaughter station after detaching the gas-delivery pipe, without transferring the stunned poultry to another container.

22. The method of claim 20 or 21, wherein detachably connecting the gas-delivery pipe automatically opens a valve associated with the gas inlet.

23. The method of any of claims 20–22, wherein detaching the gas-delivery pipe automatically closes a valve associated with the gas inlet or the gas-delivery pipe.

24. The method of any of claims 20–23, further comprising verifying a sealed connection between the gas-delivery pipe and the container before initiating the supply of stunning gas.

25. The method of any of claims 20–24, further comprising monitoring a gas concentration or oxygen concentration within the container and controlling the supply of stunning gas in response to the monitored concentration.

26. The method of any of claims 20–25, wherein the stunning gas is supplied sequentially to a plurality of containers by detaching the gas-delivery pipe from a first container and subsequently attaching the gas-delivery pipe to a second container.

27. The method of any of claims 20–25, wherein stunning gas is supplied concurrently to a plurality of containers through respective detachably connected gas-delivery pipes.

28. The method of any of claims 20–27, wherein the detachable connection allows the container to be introduced into and removed from a stunning location independently of the gas-supply system.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
